title: firsthour-incident-log-and-stepwise-gpu-swap-playbook-draft
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a first-hour focused playbook and working draft for: unexpected GPU failures, emergency GPU cartridge/hotplug replacement, node cordon & drain for degraded nodes, fast cluster recovery, and short-term capacity add to avoid customer-facing throttles.

Audience: on-call SREs, on-call infra engineers, site-reliability triage lead.
Status: working draft — contains TODOs and heuristics we should validate in the lab before automating.

High-level goals in the first 60 minutes: 
- Contain user impact (route around degraded capacity, reduce risk of noisy neighbor eviction).
- Stabilize cluster (cordon & controlled drain of bad node).
- Return capacity quickly (temp nodes or spare pool).
- Capture evidence for postmortem.

Immediate alerts & what they usually mean:
- alert: GPU-PCIe-Error-Rate (high) => possible hardware degradation or firmware; may escalate to full GPU hang.
- alert: pod-oom-gpu/eviction spike => capacity shortage, possible silent failures.
- alert: node-ready-false + kubelet down => node-level crash, may require physical intervention.
- alert: inference-tail-latency-spike with token drop => routing backlog, consider shedding non-critical work.

Quick triage (first 5-10m):
- Check current capacity: kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep gpu
- Check per-model QPS and error spikes in Dashboard (Console -> Routes -> latencies)
- Identify impacted customers / routes and notify product-oncall channel (#prod-incident or #platform-incidents).
- If node shows hardware errors: SSH to node (jump-host), run dmesg | tail -n 200; sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 200; sudo nvidia-smi -q || echo "nvidia-smi failed".

Containment actions (0-15m):
1) Cordon the node to stop new pods: kubectl cordon <node-name>  # quick and reversible
2) If pods are unhealthy or stuck, drain with care: kubectl drain <node-name> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --pod-selector='app!=infra-daemon'  # keep infra daemons
   - If drain hangs, check for local-pv or finalizers. Use kubectl patch to remove finalizer as a last resort (document and ticket).
3) If cross-zone capacity is available, shift heavier traffic via routing policy: update route weights in the Console to prefer healthy zones.
4) If we expect replacement will take >30m, trigger temporary capacity add (see Capacity add section).

Physical GPU hot-swap checklist (for coloc or bare-metal racks) — preliminary notes:
- Safety first: coordinate with data center/ops. ESD strap, coordinate power. Schedule a short maintenance window if necessary.
- Pre-swap steps (remote): drain node, ensure no critical data left, stop kubelet: sudo systemctl stop kubelet
- Power maintenance mode on BMC: ipmitool chassis power soft off (if warm swap not supported use controlled shutdown).
- Physically replace cartridge/module per vendor guide. We need vendor-specific microchecklist in 
  - TODO: add A100 PCIe vs SXM hot-swap steps (driver unload order).
- Post-swap checks (remote): power on node, validate BMC/BIOS logs, boot to known kernel; validate GPU visible: sudo nvidia-smi -L and sudo nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,serial,driver_version --format=csv
- Reinstall/verify drivers if kernel modules missing: sudo modprobe nvidia; check containerd and nvidia-container-runtime logs.
- Start kubelet: sudo systemctl start kubelet; verify node Ready and gpu allocatable reported: kubectl describe node <node> | grep -A3 Allocatable
- Draining rollback: make sure kubelet registers container runtime resources; if pods stuck in Pending, investigate tolerations and GPU resource classes.

Cloud instance GPU replacement (AWS/GCP):
- For ASG/MIG-backed GPU nodes, prefer lifecycle replace: set ASG desired+1 or increase MIG size to add new instances before terminating old ones.
- Example (AWS): aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name gpu-pool --desired-capacity $((current+1))
- For ephemeral failures, create new instance with same AMI and attach to ASG; after it becomes Ready, de-register old instance.
- If instance hardware fault needs vendor-engagement, capture instance console output and open cloud provider support case.

Cluster recovery & rebalancing (15-45m):
- Once node is Ready, confirm GPU drivers and that kubelet reports allocatable GPUs.
- Rebalance heavy pods: use kubectl get pods -o wide --sort-by=.status.startTime and check node distribution.
- If pods were force-evicted, ensure that model caches warm up sequentially (avoid thundering herd): reintroduce traffic to node gradually via routing weight ramp.
- Validate latency and error rates for affected routes for 30m after recovery.

Capacity add (fast path) — two supported approaches: temporary ASG bump OR warm spare pool: 
1) Fast ASG bump (recommended when terraform changes would take too long): scale ASG/MIG desired count +2, wait for instances to pass node readiness checks, then shift traffic.
2) Warm spare pool (longer term): maintain a standby pool in region with minimal scale-to-zero policy. To bring online: label nodes with gpu=standby and run warmup job that pre-pulls models.

Commands examples (lab-tested to copy/paste):
- cordon: kubectl cordon gpu-node-24
- drain safely: kubectl drain gpu-node-24 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60 --timeout=10m
- check gpu: ssh ops@gpu-node-24 'sudo nvidia-smi -L; sudo nvidia-smi --query-gpu=temperature.gpu,utilization.gpu --format=csv'
- scale ASG (aws cli): aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name gpu-pool --desired-capacity 18
- scale MIG (gcloud): gcloud compute instance-groups managed resize gpu-mig --size 6 --zone us-west1-b

Evidence collection (first hour, required):
- Save output: dmesg > /tmp/incident-dmesg.txt; sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 500 > /tmp/kubelet.log; sudo nvidia-smi -q > /tmp/nvidia-smi-q.txt
- Capture pod logs: kubectl logs pod/<pod> -n inference > /tmp/pod-<pod>.log
- Snapshot metrics span: download 30m graphs from Console (latency, GPU util, GPU memory pressure).
- Attach artifacts to Jira: SRE-4128 (create if absent) and tag the incident channel.

Fallbacks and graceful degradation:
- If capacity cannot be restored quickly, shift non-critical routes to latency-first model variants, enable rate-limiting per-customer to preserve fairness.
- Consider temporary disablement of batched background evals and other low-priority jobs.

Post-incident and follow-ups:
- Create incident timeline within 24h; include exact commands run, timestamps, and everyone involved.
- Postmortem due in 72h (template: Confluence->SRE->Incidents).
- Actions to consider: add a warm spare pool, automate cordon+notify step, implement a self-healing probe that will automatically scale ASG when GPU allocators drop by X%.
- Validate driver compatibility matrix across SKUs (A100, H100, V100) and maintain a vendor-compatible hot-swap checklist per SKU.

Playbook validation / runbook tests (lab tasks):
- Weekly: exercise cordon/drain on a non-prod cluster and measure time to drain with models of various sizes.
- Monthly: rehearse a physical hot-swap in staging with vendor tech support present.
- Quarterly: simulate 20% cluster GPU loss and observe routing failover behavior.

Notes-to-self / open questions (to discuss at SRE retro):
- Can we safely unload nvidia modules for warm swap or do we require full power cycle? Vendor answers vary.
- Can we add a dedicated warm-pool autoscaler that pre-warms models on spare nodes?
- Should the initial cordon be automated for GPU error alerts that reach threshold X? (pros/cons: faster containment vs. false-positive churn)
- TODO: add exact SSH/jump-host steps and hardware serial retrieval steps for each colo partner (Packet, Equinix, etc.).

Contacts & escalation
- Primary oncall: see rota in #sre-oncall (use /oncall whoami)
- Data center ops pager: ops-dc@redwood.ai, phone: +1-415-555-0212 (staging number)
- Vendor support (NVIDIA partner): partner-ticket link and SLA information in Confluence

Appendix A: quick checklist (first hour)
- [ ] Identify impacted routes & notify #platform-incidents
- [ ] Cordon node
- [ ] Drain node safely or mark for immediate replacement
- [ ] Trigger temporary capacity add if needed
- [ ] Capture logs (dmesg, kubelet, nvidia-smi)
- [ ] Confirm model warmup strategy for newly added nodes
- [ ] Create Jira and start timeline

Appendix B: quick links
- Console route dashboard -> link (Console -> Routes)
- SRE incident template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Incident+Template
- Infra terraform repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra

-- end draft --

Reminder: this doc is intentionally informal. Mark any step that becomes repetitive for automation and push small scripts into infra/ops-scripts with PR references.
